name: Alkali metal
description: Soft, shiny metals with 1 outer electron they give away easily. They react with water, some of them violently, so they never occur pure in nature.

name: Alkaline earth metal
description: Metals with 2 outer electrons. Reactive but calmer than alkali metals, and common in rocks, shells and bones.

name: Transition metal
description: The classic metals: strong, shiny, good conductors of heat and electricity, and often the source of bright colors in paints, gems and fireworks.

name: Post-transition metal
description: Softer metals with lower melting points. Great for alloys, solder and coatings.

name: Metalloid
description: Part metal, part nonmetal. Many are semiconductors, which is why they sit inside nearly every electronic device.

name: Reactive nonmetal
description: The builders of life. They share or gain electrons to form molecules like water, sugar, proteins and DNA.

name: Halogen
description: 7 outer electrons, just one short of a full shell, so they are very reactive. 'Halogen' means 'salt-former': with metals they make salts.

name: Noble gas
description: A full outer shell means they barely react with anything. They glow in bright colors when electricity passes through them.

name: Lanthanide
description: The 'rare earth' metals. Small amounts power strong magnets, screen colors, lasers and fiber optics.

name: Actinide
description: All radioactive. The family includes nuclear fuels; most members are made in reactors or particle accelerators.

name: Superheavy (properties uncertain)
description: Made a few atoms at a time in particle accelerators. They decay in seconds or less, so most of their properties are predictions.
